notes: Historical revenue and EBIT are from Steel Dynamics FY2023-FY2025 consolidated statements of income; EBIT is proxied by operating income (values converted from 'in thousands' to full dollars). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

D&A and capex use cash flow statement lines 'Depreciation and amortization' and 'Purchases of property, plant and equipment' (absolute values converted from thousands to dollars). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

NWC is constructed from balance-sheet totals: (Total current assets − cash & equivalents − short-term investments) − (Total current liabilities − current maturities of long-term debt). This includes income taxes payable and accrued items as part of working capital by construction. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

Cash uses 'Cash and equivalents' only; investments uses short-term investments (0 in FY2025). Debt uses current maturities of long-term debt + long-term debt. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))
Minority interest is set equal to 'Redeemable noncontrolling interests' at Dec 31, 2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

NOL balance is set to net operating loss carryforwards disclosed in the deferred tax footnote; NOL utilization percent is an assumption (not explicitly provided as a single utilization factor). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

Comps: EV/NTM revenue and true EV/NTM EBITDA were not available from the captured peer-multiples source; EV/EBITDA and P/E are used as the closest available anchors and EV/NTM revenue is set to null. ([alphaspread.com](https://www.alphaspread.com/security/nasdaq/stld/relative-valuation/ratio/enterprise-value-to-ebitda))
WACC, terminal growth, and terminal exit EBITDA multiple are model assumptions for DCF (not explicitly stated as final inputs in company filings).

catalysts: Improving steel and scrap market spreads that translate into higher operating margins.

Upside from aluminum/flat-roll and other expansion ramp-ups and utilization improvements as noted in the company’s latest outlook materials. ([s27.q4cdn.com](https://s27.q4cdn.com/542031646/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/earnings-result/4Q-2025-Supplemental-Financial-Information.pdf?utm_source=openai))
Capital allocation updates (share repurchases/dividend) driven by free cash flow generation.
company_overview: Steel Dynamics is a major U.S. producer of steel products with integrated downstream fabrication and metals recycling exposure.
Results are driven by steel/recycling spreads, shipment volumes, and input costs (notably scrap and energy).
The company has a large capital program tied to capacity expansions and facility improvements across divisions.
current_context: For FY2025, Steel Dynamics reported consolidated net sales of $18.18B and operating income (EBIT proxy) of $1.48B, down from FY2024 as metal spread compression weighed on profitability. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

Management highlighted record steel shipments during 2025 and stable underlying domestic demand, with operating performance affected by metal spreads. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926021395/stld-20251231x10k.htm))

The latest annual results materials include forward-looking operating outlook/guidance details in supplemental attachments. ([ir.steeldynamics.com](https://ir.steeldynamics.com/steel-dynamics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-annual-2025-results/?utm_source=openai))
investment_highlights: DCF base case assumes modest revenue growth from ongoing demand and capacity utilization while avoiding aggressive cyclic expansion.
EBIT margin recovery is modeled as mean reversion from FY2024/FY2025 spread compression toward a more normalized level by the terminal year.
Capital intensity is reflected through a sustained (but normalized) capex rate relative to sales, supporting long-run productivity and capacity.
Working capital intensity is modeled as stable to slightly improving, consistent with a mature, high-turnover manufacturing/recycling profile.
key_risks: Downside from further metal spread compression or weaker construction/manufacturing demand.
Cost inflation (scrap, energy, labor) that outpaces selling price/metal spread recovery.
Execution and cyclicality risk around capex projects (timing, ramp, and utilization).

valuation_summary: Selected DCF structure uses operating cash earnings dynamics (EBIT margin) with explicit D&A, capex, and working capital assumptions.

Terminal value relies on an exit multiple that is consistent with market EV/EBITDA ranges for steel/recycling-related peers (conservatively centered). ([alphaspread.com](https://www.alphaspread.com/security/nasdaq/stld/relative-valuation/ratio/enterprise-value-to-ebitda))
